subsystems.name: Tactile capture
subsystems.role: records touch, pressure, texture and temperature at the source.

subsystems.name: Haptic output
subsystems.role: reproduces touch sensations on the user's skin.

subsystems.name: Olfactory capture
subsystems.role: detects and digitises odours into a data pattern.

subsystems.name: Olfactory display
subsystems.role: synthesises and releases scents on demand.

subsystems.name: Neural stimulation
subsystems.role: bypasses the senses and directly stimulates sensory nerves.

subsystems.name: Network and codec
subsystems.role: transmits multisensory data with low latency.

buildSteps.title: Develop high-fidelity tactile sensors
buildSteps.detail: Create flexible pressure-sensor arrays that can map texture, force and temperature across a surface.

buildSteps.title: Build wearable haptic actuators
buildSteps.detail: Assemble arrays of vibrotactile, thermal and electrotactile elements that can be worn on the skin and driven individually.

buildSteps.title: Create an electronic nose
buildSteps.detail: Combine chemical sensor arrays with machine learning to classify volatile compounds into reproducible odour signatures.

buildSteps.title: Develop a scent synthesizer
buildSteps.detail: Build a device that mixes and atomises a set of primary odorants to recreate a target smell on demand.

buildSteps.title: Build a taste interface
buildSteps.detail: Pair chemical sensors for taste with a safe electrical or thermal stimulator that can produce basic tastes on the tongue.

buildSteps.title: Integrate neural stimulation (optional route)
buildSteps.detail: If pursuing direct neural input, develop electrode arrays that can safely stimulate specific sensory nerves with enough precision.

buildSteps.title: Develop codecs and network protocols
buildSteps.detail: Write algorithms to compress and stream multisensory data over low-latency links, prioritising the signals humans notice most.

buildSteps.title: Test in closed loop
buildSteps.detail: Send signals from a capture rig to an output rig over a network, then refine the encoding until the sensation feels natural.

buildSteps.title: Miniaturise and scale
buildSteps.detail: Make the hardware wearable, power-efficient and safe for everyday consumer use.

prerequisites.why: real-time multisensory data needs sub-10 ms latency and high reliability, which current 5G provides only in ideal conditions.
vibrotactile feedback is common, but fine texture, force and temperature reproduction remain limited.
no device can yet synthesise a wide range of odours accurately and repeatably on demand.
electrical stimulation can produce basic tastes, but complex flavours and reliable reproduction are not solved.
safe, precise stimulation of specific sensory nerves is not yet possible outside limited lab experiments.
machine learning can classify some sensory patterns, but encoding and decoding all senses in real time is unsolved.

pathway.milestone: basic haptic feedback in VR/AR (controllers, vests, gloves)
pathway.unlocks: more immersive gaming and training, but only touch is transmitted.

pathway.milestone: multisensory VR with limited scent and taste (cartridge-based scent, electrical tongue stimulation)
pathway.unlocks: richer remote experiences for media, marketing and some therapy.

pathway.milestone: wearable full-body haptic suits and compact scent/taste devices
pathway.unlocks: remote presence for meetings, healthcare and social interaction.

pathway.milestone: direct neural interfaces that bypass the sensory organs
pathway.unlocks: true telepresence, but only if neuroscience and safe implants advance dramatically.
